checks.name: api-does-not-import-the-scheduler
checks.summary: A3, the api half: PASSED. A go/parser scan over internal/api's own non-test *.go files fails if any of them imports internal/scheduler. The matcher was verified first against two known-positive paths (the exact path and a subpackage) and four known-negative ones, including a path that merely starts with the same letters (internal/schedulerless), and a synthetic file that does import the scheduler is proven to be flagged. The scan reuses apiPackageImports, which fails outright on a zero-file scan, so it cannot pass vacuously; it covered 4 non-test files and found no edge. The forbidden path is assembled from internalPackagePrefix rather than written as one literal, because internal/ci's manifest derivation reads module-path literals in source text and a literal here would create the very edge the guard denies. internal/scheduler's own import allowlist from V2-030 (TestSchedulerImportsAreStdlibOrDomainOnly, TestImportAllowlistMatcherRejectsKnownBadImportsAndAcceptsDomain, TestImportAllowlistsAreExercised) still passes unchanged, which is what proves the edge could only ever point into the scheduler.

A SECOND MEASURED CONSTRAINT, recorded because it shaped the code: every sibling block's owner.js scan slices from its own marker comment to the END of the file, so any token one of them refuses is refused in every block appended after it. The request body is therefore assembled by explicit quoting rather than with the structured serialiser.
